slot.brief: Indefinite integral of the form ∫dx/(a sin x + b cos x) or ∫(sin/cos power mix) via t = tan(x/2) or a simple substitution; easy with the right trick.

verdicts.working: Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(2+\cos x)=-\sin x\), the integral is \(-\ln(2+\cos x)+C\).

working:
$u=2+\cos x,\quad du=-\sin x\,dx$; $\displaystyle\int\frac{\sin x}{2+\cos x}\,dx=-\int\frac{du}{u}=-\ln(2+\cos x)+C$.

Independent check: Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(2+\cos x)=-\sin x\), the integral is \(-\ln(2+\cos x)+C\).
solution:
Let $u=2+\cos x$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$. Then
$$\int\frac{\sin x}{2+\cos x}\,dx=-\int\frac{du}{u}=-\ln(2+\cos x)+C.$$
